detail: 90 readings reported in order with correct temperatures
finalText:
## Root cause

`sensor_task` put `char *` pointers on the queue, all pointing at its single stack buffer `line`:

```c
char line[48];
...
snprintf(line, sizeof line, "seq=%" PRIu32 " temp=%d.%02d", ...);
char *msg = line;
xQueueSend(readings, &msg, ...);   // queues the pointer, not the text
```

The queue only stored the pointer, so every queued item aliased the same buffer. `report_task` copies nothing when it receives — it waits 30 ms and then prints whatever the buffer holds *at print time*. The sensor (higher priority) had already overwritten `line` with the last sample of the burst, so each burst printed the same final `seq`/`temp` five times (e.g. `seq=39` ×5, `seq=44` ×5), and the intermediate readings were never reported. Reproduced on hardware before the fix.

## Fix (`main/main.c`)

- Queue now carries the message **by value**: created with item size `MSG_LEN` (48 bytes) via `xQueueCreate(QUEUE_LEN, MSG_LEN)`.
- `sensor_task` sends `&line` (a copy of the text is made into the queue), so the buffer can be safely reused.
- `report_task` receives into its own `char msg[MSG_LEN]` before delaying/printing.
- `QUEUE_LEN` set to `FIFO_BURST` (5) so a full burst always fits.

Burst size (5), burst interval (500 ms), and the `report seq=<n> temp=<t>` format are unchanged.

## Verification on the board

After reflashing, `serial_capture.py` over 12 s printed 120 reports: `seq=0 temp=20.00` through `seq=119`, strictly consecutive, no gaps, and zero "queue full … dropped" warnings.
